correctness.rationale: All 511 nonempty subsets are checked against the 12 explicitly generated affine lines. The resulting 171 faces have vector (9,36,72,54). The 79 specified cover pairs are disjoint and directed-Hasse acyclicity is verified by a topological sort over all 171 vertices and 504 incidences. Exactly one degree-zero, one degree-two and eleven degree-three critical cells survive. Independent exact integral unit-pivot chain cancellation eliminates all 79 pairs and leaves zero Morse differential. Since the resulting two-skeleton is a single sphere and degree-three attaching maps lie in pi_2(S^2)=Z, zero integral degrees imply they are nullhomotopic; the claimed wedge follows. A GF(2) matrix-rank cross-check is supplementary, not a proof of integral structure.

value.rationale: The Hesse configuration is a canonical highly symmetric nine-point incidence geometry, equivalently the affine plane of order three and the flex configuration of a smooth cubic. The natural complex of all line-free subsets has homotopy information not determined by its maximum cap size, f-vector, or the homology of the projective analogue. Identifying its full mixed-dimensional sphere-wedge type gives a usable topological invariant of a classical cap system and a concrete finite model for contrasting affine and projective cap topology; the nontrivial two-sphere plus eleven three-spheres is not a textbook corollary of the cited geometric incidence facts.
